scope: Next slice continuing from docs/requirements.md: the already-given capacity — "the first board exports one SVG from local data" — is taken as settled context; this slice only decides which of the below candidate shapes editing-and-export takes. No GUI, stack, or persistence choice is invented here.
question: Which slice is next, given that the interaction style for editing is still undecided: build export-from-local-data first, or block everything on the editing decision?

options.label: Do the export slice now, editing untouched
options.tradeoff: Delivers the only settled requirement (one SVG exported from local data) without guessing the undecided editing interaction. Costs: the editing slice lands later and may reshape some of the same output path; meanwhile no editing behavior exists at all, which 'Editing is requested' will eventually require.
options.acceptanceExample: Given local data in the repository-described form, invoking the export routine produces exactly one SVG file; invoking again overwrites that one file rather than creating a second; no editing interface is shipped in this slice.

source.quote: The first board exports one SVG from local data.

options.label: Decide editing interaction before any slice
options.tradeoff: Treats the undecided interaction as a blocker so the export path is designed once, with edit hooks in place from the start. Costs: 'The first board exports one SVG from local data' is already requested and would stay undelivered while waiting; the decision itself needs a person, per INSTRUCTIONS §5, so this option delivers nothing until a respondent answers.
options.acceptanceExample: No running code in this slice; deliverable is a decision request naming the interaction-style options. Success condition: an operator records an interaction-style choice; export+editing work proceeds as one integrated slice afterward.

source.quote: Editing is requested, but its interaction style is undecided.

options.label: Export slice with a data boundary reserved for editing
options.tradeoff: Do the export slice now but keep the board model as a plain data structure handed to the exporter, so a later interaction slice plugs into that boundary without touching the SVG path. Costs: slightly more abstraction than the pure export slice, and the interaction style remains undecided — the boundary is reserved, not implemented.
options.acceptanceExample: Same export acceptance as export-first, plus: the exporter consumes only a board data structure (no assumptions about where edits came from), verified by exporting one fixed board constructed directly in code with no editing step.

source.quote: Editing is requested, but its interaction style is undecided.
